hyps.why: With edge 5 already removed, deleting edge 4 leaves only edge 3 into the output, so the loss of paths and capacity is much more damaging.
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 5 leaves the output fed only by the direct edge 3, hurting far more than when edge 4 is present.
Removing the direct input-output path is worse when fewer alternative paths into node 3 remain.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is zero, so a conv on edge 1->3 contributes nothing.
Without edge 4, node 1 influences the output only indirectly through node 2, diluting the benefit of improving edge 0.
When edge 5 is none, node 2's output is discarded, so edge 1 becomes dead and its op is irrelevant.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, whose only exit is edge 5, so it is dead when edge 5 is none.
Turning a missing edge into the best operation gains more than upgrading an existing operation.
Replacing the strongest op with a parameter-free pool loses more than replacing weaker ops.
Restoring the direct path with the best op yields a larger gain than replacing an op that already provides a path.
